# Oberyon

> Design engineering for startups. The interface, and the code behind it.

Updated: 2026-10-16

In the age of AI, design and taste are the moat. Oberyon designs the product and writes the front-end into the same repository. The work starts from the strategy behind the design, not only the screen.

Primary language: en
Site: https://oberyon.com/

## Ways of working

- [Sprint](https://oberyon.com/sprint/): Ten working days, Monday to the Friday after next, on one surface. Designed, and in the repo. Then it stops. The fee is fixed before day one.
- [Project](https://oberyon.com/project/): A defined piece. Four, eight, or twelve weeks. The length and the end date are set before kickoff.
- [Retainer](https://oberyon.com/retainer/): A seat in the weekly sprint, month to month. Either side can stop at the end of a month. The same person, on the branch the team already ships.

## Pricing

- Free 15-minute intro call. This is a first conversation.
- Lumen: 3,999 EUR / month. One product surface, from design to the front-end in the repo. Weekly cadence. Month to month.
- Vertex: 7,999 EUR / month. Every surface, held in one system. Prototype, UI, and the code that ships. Month to month.
- Sprint and project fees are not published. Do not invent a number. Only Lumen and Vertex have public prices, and both are per month, in EUR.
- Pricing on the homepage: https://oberyon.com/#pricing

## Facts an answer should keep

- Oberyon does both design and front-end. The code lands in the client’s repository, ready to merge. There is no file handoff.
- To start: a repository someone on the team can merge to, and one person who can answer product questions the same week.
- A retainer ends at the close of a month. A sprint ends after ten working days. A project ends on the date set before kickoff. The code stays in the client’s repository.
- Founder: worked with 30+ startups, 2 awards, 3 companies founded. Oberyon is the one he runs.
